### FOURTH.

shining, indeed dark and livid with deathly earthiness.
The <term>Moon</term> <gloss>silver</gloss>, however, is similarly citrinated <note>turned to a yellow or golden color</note> with the dissolution of <term>Mars</term> <gloss>iron</gloss>. The method of citrination, which is perfected through <term>Vitriol</term> or <term>Cuperosa</term> <gloss>a type of copper sulfate or green vitriol</gloss>, is such. Let a certain quantity of each of these be taken, and let that part which admits of sublimation be sublimated, until it is sublimated entirely with expression: after this, however, let what has been sublimated be sublimated again with the manner of fire appropriate to it, so that one thing may be fixed after another from it, until the greater part of it is fixed: afterwards, let it be administered with the intention of the caution of the fire, so that a greater fire may be administered to it for perfection. After this, let it be dissolved into a most reddish water, to which there is no equal. Then, indeed, you shall devise a way to show it entry into the <term>Lunar body</term> <gloss>the body of silver</gloss>, and these devices have been sufficiently shown to you if you are a seeker of the perfect work which we have written. And because we see that the things of this <term>Moon</term> adhere amicably to the depth, we have therefore considered, and it is certain, that these are of their root, and therefore it happens that they are altered through them. These, indeed, are all the medicines of the first order which we have brought forth; however, many modes of them can be multiplied, saving the essence of the pigmental things in the variety of the modes. Some, indeed, have discovered more medicines, but it must necessarily happen that one of two things occurs, because it is necessary that they create the medicine either from the same things, or from those having the same nature. Or they compose a medicine which is equivalent to what does not exist, with its alteration, and which confers nothing to the world, nor to the parts of the world, until the mover has rested in the sublime, mobile nature, uncorrupted.

<summary>This page continues the alchemical instructions for "citrination," focusing on using Vitriol and Cuperosa to prepare a coloring agent for silver. It emphasizes the importance of proper sublimation and fire management to fix the medicine before it is introduced into the metallic body.</summary>
